newsitem.title: USA: Commercial Intertech sees Q4 oper income up.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Intertech sees Q4 oper income up.

text.p: Commercial Intertech Corp said on Tuesday it expected operating income for the fourth quarter would likely exceed income in the same period last year, but fall below expectations.
This was due to a a continuing slump in many of the industry segments served by its hydraulic systems group, the company said.

Commercial Intertech also said it was negotiating with the German government to obtain operating subsidies for an underperforming unit bought from the former Treuhandanstalt. If talks failed, it said it could post a charge in 1996.
Treuhandanstalt was a German government agency which had overseen the privatization of East German companies.
The charge would reflect the costs of exiting this aspect of the German hydraulic business, the company said.

1996 results would also include a $4 million extraordinary charge net of tax for the write-off of fees and costs from a refinancing to fund a share repurchase program and the spin-off of its fluid purification business, the company said.
Commercial Intertech said it expected operating income, excluding non-recurring costs, for the fiscal year ended October 31 would be somewhat above 1995 operating income.
But, as previously announced, including $6.9 million in non-recurring after tax costs, 1996 income would be substantially below income earned last year, it said.
This shortfall was mostly attributable to the costs incurred to defend against a hostile takeover attempt and to reorganize core businesses.

The company said its metal stamping and building systems operating units would post strong results in the fourth quarter. The hydraulic unit had performed below expectations due to weak demand in certain segments, including construction, refuse and mining and truck order rates.
